claim.quote: An improved value for the lifetime of the (anti-)hypertriton has been obtained using the data sample of Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 5.02 TeV collected by the ALICE experiment at the LHC.

date.locator: arXiv:1907.06906, submitted 16 July 2019; Phys. Lett. B 797 (2019) 134905

name: (Anti-)hypertriton lifetime measurement in Pb-Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV
notes: This is an ALICE-specific hypertriton lifetime measurement; a separate, unrelated STAR-experiment hypertriton mass-difference/CPT paper (also on arXiv, coincidentally an adjacent id) was found during research and explicitly excluded from this record after its full text showed it used STAR detector data, not ALICE.

summary.plain: ALICE measured how long a rare, fragile nucleus called the hypertriton survives before decaying, using lead-lead collisions at the LHC. The collaboration reports a value compatible with representative theoretical predictions, contributing to the solution of a longstanding puzzle over this lifetime.
summary.technical: ALICE measurement of the (anti-)hypertriton lifetime via its charged two-body mesonic decay channel in Pb–Pb collisions at √sNN = 5.02 TeV: τ = 242 +34/−38 (stat) ± 17 (syst) ps, compatible with representative theoretical predictions and, in the collaboration's words, contributing to the solution of the longstanding hypertriton lifetime puzzle.

title: ³ΛH and ³Λ̄H̄ lifetime measurement in Pb–Pb collisions at √sNN = 5.02 TeV via two-body decay
why_it_matters: The hypertriton (a proton, neutron and Lambda hyperon bound together) is the lightest hypernucleus. Its Lambda is only weakly bound, so the paper cites calculations expecting a lifetime close to that of a free Lambda, while earlier heavy-ion measurements came out lower: the 'hypertriton lifetime puzzle'. The paper links hypernuclear lifetimes to the hyperon-nucleon interaction, which matters for models of neutron-star interiors.
